triage.note: S2/ADR-027. The deployed inspector reported `build unknown`, so nobody could tell which build they were looking at, and the S2 row is explicit that a hand-set env var is the wrong fix because it goes stale on every redeploy while still reading as authoritative — 'a lying build label is worse than build unknown'. The fix injects the sha at BUILD time (Zeabur exposes ZEABUR_GIT_COMMIT_SHA in the build phase only) and reads it back at runtime, which makes the honesty question mechanical: the build can hand the runtime an EMPTY file (`printf %s "$FOO"` with FOO unset), an UNEXPANDED literal (`$ZEABUR_GIT_COMMIT_SHA`), or a placeholder word, and every one of those must resolve to `unknown` rather than become a build label. That is what NOT_A_SHA in src/repo_hygiene/eval_adapter.py feeds through the real resolver — `src/sec10k/web/build_id.py` is stdlib-only and imports no fastapi precisely so this case can call it for real (ADR-003: the CI jobs install nothing, `import fastapi` fails there outright). The precedence is exercised too, not asserted in prose: the build-written file outranks a hand-set GIT_SHA, GIT_SHA still answers where no build wrote a file, and a checkout with a .git still reports its own short sha. The three things no eval can run — the Zeabur build itself — are pinned as text instead: the `build_command` in zbpack.json (pinned WHOLE, the WIRE_UI argument: a check that merely ASKS whether the command mentions the variable is answerable by a command that writes the wrong thing), the .gitignore line and the not-tracked check that keep the injected file out of the repo, and /api/meta calling the shared resolver rather than growing a second copy.
triage.what_this_cannot_prove: That Zeabur's builder actually sets ZEABUR_GIT_COMMIT_SHA, runs `build_command` in the directory the runtime later serves from, and carries the written file into the run image. No agent can run a Zeabur build. The failure mode if any of that is false is the honest one and not a regression: BUILD_SHA is absent or empty, the resolver rejects it, and /api/meta reports `unknown` exactly as it does today. Confirmed only by curling /api/meta after the human merges and Zeabur redeploys.
triage.red_first: Three reds, all observed. (1) The env-var-only resolver this repo shipped, with no build_command: 8 failures — no injected sha is read at all and the zbpack/.gitignore pins are unsatisfied. (2) The naive file-first resolver that reads BUILD_SHA back without asking what is in it: 12 failures — ten values a build can produce with NO human error became build labels, truncated to twelve characters and served as identity ('$ZEABUR_GIT', '${ZEABUR_GIT', 'HEAD', 'main', 'latest', 'a1b2c3', 'zzzzzzz', 'a1b2c3d4-dir', 'a1b2 c3d4e5f', and a 41-hex near-miss). That is the red that made validation part of ADR-027's ruling rather than an implementation detail. (3) The one that paid for itself: the FIRST run of this case inside the pre-commit hook reported 16 failures on an implementation green everywhere else. `git rev-parse` honours GIT_DIR from the environment and git SETS it while running a hook, so the resolver answered with the repo's HEAD while pointed at a temp directory that is not a repository — every NOT_A_SHA value 'resolved' to '17d43fc'. That blocked run's report is committed at evals/report/20260822-161040-fast.json (80/81) rather than left as an uncited dump. That is a defect in `git_sha`, not in the case: an inherited GIT_DIR in a container would equally make the deployed app report a stranger repo's sha. Fixed in both — the resolver runs git in the environment it was handed, and the temp-dir assertions run with PATH and nothing else while the local-dev assertion uses the real environment.
triage.refalsified: Six mutations against the fixed implementation, each built and watched red, then restored green: zbpack build_command deleted (1 failure), .gitignore entry removed (1), SHA_RE relaxed to `.+` (10), precedence flipped so GIT_SHA outranks the build (1), build_sha ignoring the file entirely (6), /api/meta growing its own private resolver again (2). Of those six, a text-level pin over app.py — the shape ui-* checks use — can see exactly ONE (the last). That measurement is why the resolver lives in a fastapi-free module the case can execute.
